message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult male lions. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion: if a male lion inherits the allele for mane growth from either parent, he will develop a mane (though its size and density can vary). This dominant trait is what gives male lions their iconic, mane‑bearing appearance.
